story.title: Una llamada de viernes
story.teaser: Marta thinks her weekend is going to be quiet and lonely, until her phone rings.
lines: Es viernes por la tarde y suena el teléfono.
It is Friday afternoon and the phone rings.
Marta mira la pantalla y sonríe.
Marta looks at the screen and smiles.
Es su amigo Javier, de Madrid.
It is her friend Javier, from Madrid.
—¡Hola, Marta! ¿Qué tal estás?
"Hi, Marta! How are you?"
—Hola, Javier. Estoy bien, pero un poco triste.
"Hi, Javier. I'm fine, but a little sad."
—¿Por qué estás triste? —pregunta él.
"Why are you sad?" he asks.
—Este fin de semana no tengo planes y voy a estar sola.
"This weekend I have no plans and I'm going to be alone."
—¿Sola? ¿Y tu familia?
"Alone? What about your family?"
—Mi familia vive lejos y mis amigas trabajan.
"My family lives far away and my friends are working."
—Entonces, ¿qué vas a hacer el sábado?
"So, what are you going to do on Saturday?"
—Voy a cocinar una tortilla y ver una película.
"I'm going to cook a tortilla and watch a movie."
—Suena aburrido —dice Javier con una sonrisa.
"That sounds boring," says Javier with a smile.
—Sí, un poco —contesta ella.
"Yes, a little," she answers.
—Marta, ¿tienes pan y queso en casa?
"Marta, do you have bread and cheese at home?"
—Sí, tengo un poco. ¿Por qué?
"Yes, I have a little. Why?"
—Porque voy a comer contigo el sábado.
"Because I'm going to eat with you on Saturday."
—¿Qué dices? ¡Tú vives en Madrid!
"What are you saying? You live in Madrid!"
—Sí, pero ahora estoy en Sevilla, delante de tu edificio.
"Yes, but right now I'm in Seville, in front of your building."
Marta corre a la ventana y ve a Javier.
Marta runs to the window and sees Javier.
Él tiene una maleta y unas flores en las manos.
He has a suitcase and some flowers in his hands.
—¡Sorpresa! Voy a pasar el fin de semana aquí —dice.
"Surprise! I'm going to spend the weekend here," he says.
Ella se ríe y baja a abrir la puerta.
She laughs and goes down to open the door.
El sábado no va a estar sola.
On Saturday she is not going to be alone.

quiz.q: ¿Qué va a hacer Marta el sábado?

story.prompt: Imagine you call a friend. Write a short dialogue in Spanish: ask what your friend is going to do on Saturday and answer with ir a + infinitive (for example: —¿Qué vas a hacer el sábado? —Voy a ver una película. ¿Y tú?).

concepts.grammar: ir a + infinitive for near plans (voy a cocinar, vas a hacer); time expressions: el sábado, ahora, mañana.
concepts.vocabulary: Phone, weekend and food words: teléfono, fin de semana, tortilla, queso, maleta.
concepts.skills: Following a two-speaker dialogue; talking about plans for the weekend.

grammar.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
grammar.explain: 'Ir a' + infinitive talks about the future, like English 'going to': voy a cocinar, vas a hacer, va a estar. Pattern: voy/vas/va/vamos/van + a + infinitive. Watch out: don't drop the 'a' ('vas hacer' is wrong), and don't conjugate the second verb ('vas a haces' is wrong).
examples: —Este fin de semana no tengo planes y voy a estar sola.
"This weekend I have no plans and I'm going to be alone."
—Entonces, ¿qué vas a hacer el sábado?
"So, what are you going to do on Saturday?"
—Voy a cocinar una tortilla y ver una película.
"I'm going to cook a tortilla and watch a movie."

grammar.explain: Question words carry a written accent: ¿qué? (what), ¿por qué? (why), ¿dónde? (where), ¿cómo? (how), ¿cuándo? (when), ¿quién? (who). Written questions open with ¿ and close with ?. '¿Qué tal estás?' = How are you? Watch out: '¿Qué dices?' literally asks 'What are you saying?', but often shows surprise, like 'What?!'
examples: —¡Hola, Marta! ¿Qué tal estás?
"Hi, Marta! How are you?"
—¿Por qué estás triste? —pregunta él.
"Why are you sad?" he asks.
—¿Qué dices? ¡Tú vives en Madrid!
"What are you saying? You live in Madrid!"

grammar.topic: Ser for time, estar for feelings
grammar.explain: Use 'ser' for the day and the time: Es viernes, Son las dos. Use 'estar' for how you feel and where you are: Estoy bien, Estoy en Sevilla. 'Estoy' is the 'I' form of estar. Watch out: 'I'm fine' is always 'Estoy bien'; 'Soy bien' is wrong.
examples: Es viernes por la tarde y suena el teléfono.
It is Friday afternoon and the phone rings.
—Hola, Javier. Estoy bien, pero un poco triste.
"Hi, Javier. I'm fine, but a little sad."
—Sí, pero ahora estoy en Sevilla, delante de tu edificio.
"Yes, but right now I'm in Seville, in front of your building."

grammar.explain: With days of the week, Spanish uses 'el' where English uses 'on': el sábado = on Saturday. 'Los sábados' = on Saturdays (every week). Days are written in lowercase. Watch out: don't add 'en': 'en el sábado' is wrong.
examples: —Entonces, ¿qué vas a hacer el sábado?
"So, what are you going to do on Saturday?"
El sábado no va a estar sola.
On Saturday she is not going to be alone.
Los sábados como con mi familia.
On Saturdays I eat with my family.

gq.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
gq.q: Which sentence means 'What are you going to do on Saturday?'
gq.why: Ir + a + infinitive: vas a hacer. Don't drop 'a', and don't conjugate the second verb.

gq.q: Marta answers: 'Estoy bien, pero un poco triste.' What did Javier ask?
gq.why: '¿Qué tal estás?' (How are you?) asks how someone is, so 'Estoy bien' answers it. ¿Dónde? asks where; ¿Quién? asks who.

gq.topic: Ser for time, estar for feelings
gq.q: Fill in the blank: Hoy ___ viernes y yo ___ bien.
gq.why: Ser gives the day (es viernes), and estar gives how you feel (estoy bien).

gq.q: What does 'El sábado no va a estar sola' mean?
options: She was not alone on Saturday.
On Saturday she is not going to be alone.
gq.why: 'El' before a day means 'on' (this one Saturday; 'los sábados' would be every Saturday), and 'va a estar' is the near future.

gq.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
gq.q: Complete: Mañana nosotros ___ cocinar una tortilla.
gq.why: Near future = ir + a + infinitive; with nosotros: vamos a cocinar.

gq.q: Complete: —¿___ vive tu familia? —Mi familia vive lejos.
gq.why: The answer 'lejos' (far away) gives a place, so the question word is ¿Dónde? (where), with an accent.

gq.topic: Ser for time, estar for feelings
options: Está viernes y soy en Sevilla.
Es viernes y soy en Sevilla.
Es viernes y estoy en Sevilla.
gq.why: Day of the week → ser (es viernes). Where you are → estar (estoy en Sevilla). 'I'm fine' is 'Estoy bien'.

gq.q: Complete: ___ sábado voy a comer con Marta. (On Saturday…)
gq.why: Spanish uses just 'el' for 'on' with days: el sábado. 'En el sábado' is a typical English-speaker mistake.

culture.prompt: Spanish (Sevillian) setting. Location: Seville, Spain. The famous landmark La Giralda must be clearly visible and recognizable in the image. A small apartment living room in Seville, Spain on a Friday afternoon: a ringing smartphone on a table, a plate with bread and cheese and a Spanish omelette (tortilla) ready, a small vase of flowers, a window with orange trees and a whitewashed building across the street. Through the window, the Giralda bell tower of Seville Cathedral is visible over the rooftops. No people. Keep the lower-left third of the frame open (clear floor, ground or table space) so a drawn character can be added. Photorealistic photograph, natural light, soft warm color grade, slightly muted colors, eye-level camera, shallow depth of field, 4:3 landscape, high resolution. No text, no logos, no watermarks.
